items.prompt: Place n queens on an n×n chessboard so that no two attack each other, and return every such board.
items.why: Each placement must fit with the queens already placed, and most partial boards die early → backtracking with column and diagonal sets. Subsets would generate every placement, valid or not.

items.prompt: Given a grid of letters and a word, decide whether the word can be traced through adjacent cells without using a cell twice.
items.why: 'Not twice' applies per path, so the used-mark is undone when you return → backtracking. Islands/BFS visit each cell once for good, which would block other paths.

items.prompt: Count the number of ways to make an amount from unlimited coins of given denominations (amount ≤ 5000).
items.why: Only a count, with overlapping subproblems and a large amount → unbounded knapsack DP. Backtracking would enumerate every way one by one.

items.prompt: Split a string into pieces so that every piece is a palindrome, and return every possible split.
items.why: Return all splits where each cut must produce a palindrome → backtracking: choose the next piece, recurse only if it's a palindrome. The DP pattern answers 'minimum cuts', not 'list them all'.

items.prompt: Given distinct numbers, return all of their subsets.
items.why: Every combination is valid and nothing is pruned → BFS subsets from the empty set. Backtracking pays off when constraints reject partial answers.

items.prompt: Fill the empty cells of a 9×9 Sudoku so every row, column and 3×3 box has the digits 1–9.
items.why: Each digit must agree with digits placed earlier, and a dead end means undoing choices → constraint backtracking with row/column/box sets. It's a grid, but nothing is flood-filled.

items.prompt: Given up to 100 numbers, can you pick some of them (each at most once) that add up exactly to S ≤ 10⁴?
items.why: Yes/no over subsets with n = 100 (2¹⁰⁰ subsets) and a small sum → 0/1 knapsack DP over (item, sum).

items.prompt: Given a string of digits, return every way to insert three dots to make a valid IPv4 address.
items.why: Choose each octet in turn and abandon it when it's > 255 or has a leading zero → backtracking with pruning.
